The steak knife circles once above your plate, catches the lamp’s light, and settles neatly back into your hand.

Ashara watches it without much expression. “Don’t do that with the dinner knives. I need a partner who knows the drills well enough to test my timing.”

Rashid nods. “You can learn. But volunteering to be hit isn’t much of a starting qualification.”

“Accurate,” Thessaly says. “A little severe.”

“I have a ranked bout tomorrow,” Ashara says. “I’m not spending tonight teaching someone how to stand.”

Caelindra cuts another piece of roast. “A remarkably sensible decision.”

Ashara gives her a flat look, then turns back to you. “Watch tomorrow’s bout. If you still want lessons afterward, ask.”
